brief: Mulberry dusk ledger, seven projects stepping down in wide italic caps, Spaceman lit in a mint band that runs off the edge.
rationale:
The phrase is "Cut what doesn't matter. Ship what's left." It comes from the Ueshiba quote and the reading-list piece about software as sculpture, put in Doug's terms. The second sentence promises something, so the page shows what's left: seven projects, set as the largest object, biggest first. That makes it a `list` day. The phrase sits above the list as a standfirst h1 at `2xl`, and the first project title takes marquee scale. Row sizes step down the ramp from `hero` to `2xl`, which is where the accelerating rhythm comes from. It is the terracotta specimen's type waterfall applied to work titles.

A ledger has to hang off one edge, so the shell moves out of the way into a left rail. That placement has not shipped in the window and it avoids the rejected top bar. The rail carries the mark at 48px in original colours on the darkest mulberry, and a one-sentence nav. The chassis is anybody-franklin, which has not shipped in fourteen builds. Wide heavy italic caps make short project names read as built objects, and the italic gives "ship" forward lean without tipping into parody at `2xl`. Franklin answers Anybody's square grotesk skeleton in the body. Caps, italic and heavy are the type moves. Alignment stays left and texture stays none despite recency, because a ledger reads from one rail and a decorative texture would contradict the phrase. Motion is none for the same reason.

The palette follows the cut: two hues, no neutral plane. Mulberry at 304° takes the only band the mandate leaves open and suits a 4:52 sunset. Mint at 150° sits inside the mandate's target range as the ink and as the one flooded field, the Spaceman row, which runs off the right edge. Duotone is off the recent-formula list, and no ground material is used. At 360 the rail becomes a top band, the mint row goes full-bleed under the phrase, and the titles keep stepping down.

hero.copy: Cut what doesn't matter. Ship what's left.
hero.rationale:
Composed from two of today's signals that say the same thing: the Ueshiba line about losing the desire for things that do not matter, and the reading-list piece arguing that software is now closer to sculpture, where the hard part is seeing what to keep. I turned that into a working rule about Doug's own practice, two short imperatives with no adjectives, and it sets up a page where the work that is left is the largest thing on it. Lane is composed, yesterday's was signal-event, so no streak.
Owner's voice: I say what a thing does. Most of my job is deciding what comes out of a design before it gets built, then shipping the rest.

adBrief.selfCheck:
1. Hero quotability: Yes — two imperatives, seven words, readable with nothing around them.
2. Because-of chain: Yes — cutting gives a duotone with no neutrals, no texture and no motion, and "what's left" gives the work index as the object, biggest first.
3. Render feasibility: Yes — SPACEMAN at 128px is about 670px wide in an 800px track, and the h1 at `2xl` sets one sentence per line inside 1100px.
4. Canvas floor feasible: Yes — rail, hero zone, a 240px mint band and the next row fill about 75% of 1440×900.
5. Phone: Yes — band 120px plus the h1 at `2xl` in five short lines lands by about 420px, and the longest word, DOESN'T, fits 328px.

adBrief.compositionRationale: "Ship what's left" makes the work index the object, so `hero_object` moves off statement to `list`, with the phrase as its standfirst. `shell_posture` moves to `marginal` because a left rail has not shipped in the window and it gives `rail-to-band` a real rail to collapse. `symmetry` moves onto the discouraged `left-weighted` because a ledger has to hang off one left edge, which is also a standing owner rule. The remaining starting values stay because the idea needs them: horizontal rows, a waterfall that speeds up as titles shrink, three tracks (rail, title, meta), and a mint band that runs off the right edge.

colorScheme.color_story: Two hues and nothing else, because the phrase is about cutting: a mulberry ground at November dusk and one mint that lights the row that matters. The mandate's 140–180° target sits inside its own forbidden zone, so the primary takes the only open band (288–352°) and the mint second hue lands at 150° to honor the target.

shell.footer: ledger tail. One last ruled row in the same two-track grid as the day ledger, holding the identity line, contact link and year. No field reversal and no separate block.

header.nav: Left rail on the darkest mulberry, 220px wide, full page height, header block sticky in its top 320px. The 48px circular mark sits at the top with 32px of clear space above it, in original colours, with the white disc carrying 14:1 on the rail ground. Below it is one lowercase sentence in mint ink, wrapping to about four lines: "start with the work, then read about me, then get in touch." The words work, about me and get in touch are the links, underlined in mint, each line box 44px tall. There is no top bar. The mark is inside the first fold at 1440 and 360.

verdicts.feedback:
1. **Judgment 5 (copy vs records).** The deck says "Seven projects, 2008 to 2026. I designed and built each one. Biggest first." The records do not support "designed and built each one" for all seven:
   - TeeTurn's record says only "Responsible for product direction and strategy."
   - Politweets and Twittertale were built "with the Character140 collective" and "with Jason Garber and the Character140 crew."
   - Spaceman is the LLC he operates under as Founder, not a thing he designed and built.

   Cut the middle sentence so the deck reads "Seven projects, 2008 to 2026. Biggest first." at both widths. Everything else passes and should not change.

1. Judgment 5: the footer row at 360 (fold 5) reads "Doug March. Product designer and developer. Ashburn, Virginia." The work records give his name and role but no location, and the page's own eyebrow and weather row say "Aldie, Virginia". Drop "Ashburn, Virginia" from the footer and the rail foot, leaving "Doug March. Product designer and developer."
2. Judgment 6 (`nav_form: sentence`, 360): the padded inline-flex links push the punctuation away from the words, so the band reads "work , then read about me , then get in touch ." Keep the 44px targets but pull the comma and full stop tight to each link (padding on the block axis only, or negative inline margin) so it reads as one sentence, as it does in the desktop rail.

Everything else passes and should not be touched: SPACEMAN on the mint band leads inside the first fold at both 1440 and 360, the heavy italic caps ledger steps down as declared, and mulberry with mint in a left rail repeats no recent night.

SPACEMAN at marquee scale on the one mint band, running off the right edge under a quieter two-line standfirst, makes the work ledger the clear lead at both widths, and it sits fully inside the first fold at 1440 and at 360 with the titles stepping down beneath it; the left rail with its lowercase nav sentence, the duotone ground, the ledger-tail footer and the project years and kinds all match the declarations and the records.

measurables.method: Measured at 1440x900 on a 20px grid over the viewport at scroll position zero. canvas_utilization: % of grid cells touched by an element carrying designed content (visible text, an image/SVG/video/canvas, a background colour distinct from the page background and not transparent, or a background image such as a gradient). A background set on html or body counts as painting the page, unless it is opaque white; ::before and ::after boxes count on the same terms. color_coverage: % of grid cells whose sampled background, background-image stops or text colour is chromatic (HSL saturation > 12%, lightness 8-92%). hero_px: the largest computed font-size among first-fold elements that set visible text.
